sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847

items.q: The EARLIEST finding of endogenous hypercortisolism on the 8 AM plasma cortisol is:
items.exp: 8 AM plasma cortisol >1.8 µg/dl = loss of diurnal variation, the earliest finding; too low suggests exogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

items.q: The over-night dexamethasone suppression test (ONDST) is performed as:
opts: 1 mg oral dexamethasone at 11 pm, then next-day 8 AM plasma cortisol
items.exp: ONDST: 1 mg oral dexamethasone at 11 pm; next-day 8 AM cortisol <1.8 rules out, >1.8 = endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

items.q: On the ONDST, a next-morning cortisol below what value rules out Cushing's?
items.exp: <1.8 µg/dl rules out Cushing's; >1.8 µg/dl indicates endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

items.q: The low-dose DST (0.5 mg Q6H for 2 days) is reserved for:
items.exp: LDDST is used in suspected pseudocushing, obesity, hyperestrogenism, PCOS or OCP use; >1.8 µg/dl = endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

items.q: In the ACTH evaluation, a value <10 pg/ml indicates:
items.exp: ACTH <10 pg/ml = ACTH independent, adrenal cause (10%); >10 pg/ml = ACTH dependent. (Book p847)

items.q: Match ACTH-dependent levels — 1) 10–50 pg/ml  2) 50–100 pg/ml  3) >100 pg/ml … A) Both pituitary & adrenal cause  B) Paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS)  C) Pituitary cause
items.exp: 10–50 pg/ml pituitary cause; 50–100 both; >100 paraneoplastic (PNS) → PET scan. (Book p847)

items.q: For an ACTH-independent adrenal cause, the imaging step is:
items.exp: ACTH independent → CT adrenal, showing U/L adenoma or (rarely) B/L hyperplasia. (Book p847)

items.q: After bilateral adrenalectomy, loss of negative feedback risks ↑↑ACTH and an ACTH adenoma known as:
items.exp: B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy carries the risk of ↑↑ACTH (↓−ve feedback) → ACTH adenoma (Nelson syndrome). (Book p847)

items.q: Match treatment to lesion — 1) U/L adrenal adenoma  2) B/L hyperplasia  3) Pituitary adenoma (≥6 mm) … A) B/L adrenalectomy  B) Trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy  C) Unilateral adrenalectomy
items.exp: U/L adenoma → unilateral adrenalectomy; B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy; pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy. (Book p847)

items.q: On MRI brain with gadolinium, a pituitary mass of what size is taken as a pituitary adenoma directly?
items.exp: ≥6 mm mass → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <6 mm → inferior petrosal sinus sampling; no mass → PET scan. (Book p847)

items.q: When MRI shows NO pituitary mass, the next step is:
opts: PET scan; if −ve and high-dose DST +ve go to IPSS, if +ve diagnose PNS
items.exp: No mass → PET scan: −ve (with high-dose DST +ve) → inferior petrosal sinus sampling; +ve → Dx PNS. (Book p847)
